about: The one curated source for where the Tear program stands. docs/POSITION.md is rendered from this file by `pnpm position:render`, and `pnpm check:docs` fails when the rendered file is stale or was edited by hand. Each area records its state in a few words, what is true now, the next step, what only the owner can do, and evidence: repository paths that exist, or links to pull requests. Change this file in the same pull request that changes an area's state, update `curated` when you review the whole file, and re-render.

production.note: Deployed after the owner played it and said the build is good. The previous release was the 2026-08-30 build 9e7d6a70.

areas.name: Release readiness
areas.summary: Pull request 85 merged the release-readiness line on 2026-11-13 (developer surfaces gated out of release builds, menu UI rebuilt, startup payload 4.13 MB to 2.10 MB, offline cache 14.77 MB to 6.74 MB, new code-budget, determinism and architecture gates). Follow-ups 86, 87 and 89 to 92 merged the same day (runtime split, one world constructor, Prettier). The phase table in the plan still shows the pre-merge states.
areas.next: Production deploy, after the owner has played the build.

areas.name: Production deploy
areas.summary: tearblade.com runs main commit 84761549; the owner played the build and said it is good (D-013). Preview deploys continue under the 2026-11-12 standing delegation.
areas.next: The next production deploy follows the Verdant, Tutorial and music work.

areas.name: Verdant Sanctum visuals
areas.summary: The game draws Verdant itself at load from a stage art recipe (src/presentation/stage-art): a key light, an atmosphere, colour ramps and layers of shared strokes (foliage, trunks, ruined arcades, water, light), painted in short slices into layers the scene renderer composes. The painted image package is gone. Any biome reaches the same look with a recipe; Pale Traverse is next. Boss warnings and strikes on Verdant are drawn as roots and thorns rising from the floor, from a table on the stage's presentation definition that any biome can supply. The background does not move yet.
areas.next: Keep closing the look toward the owner's reference illustration, then a live layer (light shafts, water glints, sway) as recipe data, then Pale Traverse from a recipe.
areas.owner_action: Judge the drawn look against the reference illustration: the owner's taste decides visual work.

areas.name: Verdant Sanctum gameplay
areas.summary: The Rootbound boss is rebuilt in all three phases as data on a shared boss move layer that Pale and later bosses reuse: Phase I's moves, Phase II's Grafts, Root Cage and Bloom Wells, and Phase III's Regrowth and Last Spring. Its body no longer hurts on touch: it blocks, and it does not play a move the player could not walk out of. Bloom Wells, the Rootbinder and its links, and Verdant waves are not rebuilt yet.
areas.next: The Bloom Wells and Rootbinder design, then Verdant waves.
areas.owner_action: Playtest the Rootbound in all three phases.

areas.name: Tutorial and Playground experience
areas.summary: A session is reworking the Tutorial and Playground popups, menus, flow, navigation and explanations. Drills has LESSONS, WEAPONS, ENEMIES and BOSSES tabs, and its phone list is sized from its content.
areas.next: One source of names for the drilled weapon moves (this pull request, then its floaters), then the release tutorial flow and menu fixes.

areas.name: Pale Traverse rework
areas.summary: Pale Traverse stays a Playground preview and is not published. The owner wants it reworked after Verdant. Its earlier migration work is on the unmerged branch codex/pale-traverse-r4.
areas.next: Start once the Verdant gameplay rework has landed.

areas.name: Player wiki
areas.summary: The wiki moves into this repository as wiki/, built from the same commit as the game: facts come from the exporter (pnpm export:wiki), pictures from the game's own renderers and test build. The separate tear-wiki repository is archived once a deploy from here is live.
areas.next: Review the move pull request, then confirm the Cloudflare secret question and run the first wiki deploy.
areas.owner_action: Archive shaku1z/tear-wiki after the first deploy from this repository.

areas.name: Repository structure and workflow
areas.summary: Porting the structure patterns recommended by the comparison with the owner's OFFSLCT project. Merged: this generated position file, decisions and pitfalls, the repository map with size caps, the pull request and task card templates, the tool catalogue with pnpm who, change-impact completeness and release compatibility fixtures. Open: the owner guard hooks and merge helper moving into scripts/governance/.
areas.next: After the hooks pull request merges, run pnpm setup:hooks in the canonical checkout on main (scripts/governance/README.md).

areas.name: Playtest tool
areas.state: Stage 1 in part: pnpm playtest bosses prints a table per boss fight and phase, from Phase I or a chosen phase
areas.summary: One command, pnpm playtest, that plays the game headless with scripted players on fixed seeds and reports clear rates, time to kill, damage taken and differences between builds. It is built from the working parts of TearBench and the scripted player and replaces both names. Verified on 2026-11-16: the scripted player runs headless at 13 to 15 times real time and the same seed reproduces exactly.
areas.next: Rest of stage 1: the still, walker and no-dodge players, boss movement, and the sweep over weapons and seeds.

areas.name: TearBench C21 to C40 program
areas.summary: The TearBench certification program state is recorded for the production build and is still checked by check:docs. Pull request 84 (five-run canary qualification) is open; its commits are already in main.

areas.name: Mobile, touch and phone layouts
areas.summary: The owner paused all mobile work and wants it out of the official production builds until further notice. Touch controls, stick or drag aim, the rotate gate, phone layouts, touch density and haptics exist in the source. Touch-aim fixes are parked as draft pull request 191. Sessions write anything mobile will need later in plans/MOBILE_LATER.md.
areas.next: Leave the mobile code out of the production builds while keeping it in dev and test builds.
